idiom_name: Array.prototype.reduce(callback, initialValue) and reduceRight for right folds
implementation_notes: JavaScript absorbs the fold into the array prototype: reduce(callbackFn, initialValue) threads the accumulator left to right and reduceRight does the same from the end, which is the right fold and the correct spelling for a right-nesting combine over the whole array. An explicit initialValue is what makes the accumulator's type independent of the elements and what keeps the empty array from throwing TypeError; reducer composition (a fold of reducers) is the same shape one level up and is how reducer libraries express pipelines. For object- or tree-shaped data there is no prototype fold: the catamorphism is a recursive function over the nodes, which is what a structural reducer over a tree amounts to.
pitfalls: Without an initialValue the accumulator is seeded from the first element (throwing TypeError on an empty array) and its type is inferred from that element, so a heterogeneous array silently folds into a different carrier than intended.

The callback receives (accumulator, currentValue, index, array): passing a function with a different arity (parseInt, Number, a constructor) forwards the index and the array into it, which is the classic reduce-as-parseInt bug.

Mutating the array being reduced (pushing into it from inside the reducer) changes what remains to be visited; build a new carrier or collect first, and remember reduce has no short-circuit - use find/some for a stop.

variants.name: Fold over a lazy iterator pipeline (iterator helpers, ES2025)
variants.implementation_notes: ES2025's iterator helpers put the fold on the iterator protocol: Iterator.prototype.reduce(callbackFn[, initialValue]) folds any iterator, and map/filter/take/flatMap return new lazy iterators, so a fold can terminate a chain that never materialises an array and that pulls from a generator, a Map/Set iterator or a custom iterable. Unlike the other helpers reduce is not lazy - it drains the iterator, so it does not work with infinite iterators - and it throws TypeError for an empty iterator without an initialValue, exactly like the array method. Prefer it over Array.prototype.reduce when the source is a generator or a large stream where intermediate arrays are the cost; keep the array method for arrays, where it is faster because it skips the iterator protocol.
pitfalls: reduce is the one non-lazy iterator helper: the pipeline before it is lazy, but the fold drains whatever the pipeline yields, so an unbounded generator without a take/takeWhile bound never returns.
Helpers live on iterators, not iterables: an array or Set must be adapted with .values() or Iterator.from(iterable), and a consumed iterator cannot be folded again - the results are single-use.
Runtime floor: iterator helpers need Node 22+ or a 2025-era browser; on older targets the chain is a TypeError unless a polyfill or a hand-written generator fold is used.
